school: Social Psychology, Behavioral Science, Human Decision Making
legacy: Stanley Milgram became one of the most influential social psychologists of the twentieth century through his investigations into how individuals respond to authority, social expectations, and group structures. His work encouraged deeper examination of the forces that shape human behavior in social environments and helped establish new directions for research into obedience, responsibility, and interpersonal influence.
earlyLife: Stanley Milgram developed an early interest in human behavior, society, and the ways individuals relate to larger social systems. As he pursued psychological studies, he became increasingly fascinated by questions concerning conformity, authority, and decision making. These interests inspired a research career focused on understanding how ordinary people behave under social pressure.
scientificField: Psychology, Social Psychology, Behavioral Science, Human Interaction
majorContributions: Milgram contributed important insights into the relationship between individual judgment and social influence. His research explored how authority structures affect behavior, how social connections link individuals within large populations, and how people respond to responsibility within organized systems. He expanded understanding of obedience, social networks, and collective behavior while encouraging psychologists to investigate real-world social dynamics through carefully structured experimentation.
laterLife: Throughout his later career, Milgram continued exploring questions related to social interaction, communication, urban life, and human connectedness. His work broadened beyond authority and obedience to examine how individuals are linked through social networks and how social environments influence everyday decisions. His research remained influential across psychology, sociology, organizational studies, and behavioral science.
whyImportant: Stanley Milgram is important because he revealed how strongly social circumstances can influence human actions. His research challenged assumptions about independence, responsibility, and decision making while encouraging broader discussions about ethics, authority, and social systems. Many modern studies of leadership, organizational behavior, compliance, and social influence build upon questions that his work helped bring to prominence.
